context.note: Queue task 325, GH#625, stage S5. CODE-DESIGNER committed the design as e7cb21a on feature/WF02-REQ173-20260828. Hard gate -- do not rubber-stamp, per this project's track record (REQ-172's design was FAILED twice for unverified behavioral claims). Design adds a NEW module, Letflow.Engine.Wasm.ModuleVersionRegistry, a supervised singleton GenServer composing ModuleRegistry (REQ-166)/CapabilityGate (REQ-167)/PluginHandler (REQ-165/170/171/172)'s existing public functions rather than modifying those already-gate-approved modules. Key claims to independently verify: (1) register_version/3 runs ModuleRegistry.register/1's (up to 5s) validation in the CALLING process, only making one fast internal call to commit -- verify this genuinely keeps the registry's own serialized loop from blocking on a slow registration; (2) invoke/4's checkout mechanism (GenServer.call copying out an immutable version_snapshot() -- manifest + compiled module -- and incrementing a ref count) BEFORE import-table-building/instantiation is claimed to make activation-immunity a consequence of BEAM process isolation, not a discipline convention -- verify this is actually true given how the snapshot is used downstream (does anything ever reach back into the registry process for the manifest/module after checkout, which would break the isolation claim?); (3) the registry process is claimed to NEVER run guest code or ModuleRegistry.register/1's validation, so it can never be blocked by a hung invocation and activate/2 is never delayed -- verify by tracing the actual call sequence in the design; (4) reference counting: a version's resources are nulled only when non-current AND ref_count=0, checked at exactly two triggers (explicit release, or activate finding the superseded version already idle) -- verify no third path could leak or premature-release; (5) the Process.monitor-as-crash-safety-net claim (a Task.shutdown(:brutal_kill)'d hung invocation still decrements the count via :DOWN) -- verify this against REQ-170's actual, already-accepted timeout/abandonment mechanism (does a :DOWN message actually fire in that scenario, or does the design assume it without checking?); (6) capability isolation via per-version-id immutable manifests, always built from the checked-out snapshot rather than a 'current' lookup; (7) the test design's reuse of REQ-172's do_call_service/8 test-double seam as a controllable/releasable gate instead of the existing uncontrollable *_hang.wat fixtures -- verify this seam actually exists and behaves as claimed, live-check the source; (8) confirm the design contains no implementation code.

task.description: Independently validate lib/letflow/design/req173-wasm-module-hot-reload.md against every REQ-173 acceptance criterion. This is a hard gate -- if the design has a genuine defect (a false live-verification claim, an unaddressed acceptance criterion, ambiguity that would force ELIXIR-DEV to invent behavior, or implementation code where interface/@spec-level design belongs), send it back to CODE-DESIGNER with the specific defect named, do not approve it. Pay special attention to concurrency claims (checkout-before-mutation immunity, ref-counted release, monitor-based crash safety) -- these are the kind of claim that reads plausible in prose but can be subtly wrong; trace the actual proposed call sequences yourself rather than accepting the narrative.
acceptance_criteria: a test holds an invocation open (a guest blocked in a controllable host call), activates a new module version DURING it, and asserts the held invocation completes normally against the OLD version's observable behaviour -- WASM-14's own acceptance criterion, with the overlap real rather than sequential
the same test asserts an invocation started AFTER the activation observes the NEW version's behaviour, so both halves of WASM-14 are proven in one overlapping scenario
the two module versions used are observably different in output, so the test can distinguish which version served an invocation rather than merely completing
a test asserts the prior version's resources are released only after its last in-flight invocation completes, not at activation time

a test asserts that when the new version's manifest declares a DIFFERENT capability set, an in-flight invocation of the prior version keeps the prior version's capability set, and the new invocation gets the new one -- so activation cannot silently widen or narrow a running invocation's authority
mix test and mix compile --warnings-as-errors both pass with real output quoted
